sections.html:
Happy Valley is a suburban city in the northwest corner of Clackamas County, about 13 miles southeast of downtown Portland. It covers roughly 12 square miles and borders Portland, Clackamas, Sunnyside and the area that used to be the City of Damascus. The land rises toward Mount Scott, an extinct volcano that tops out near 1,050 feet, and large parts of Scouters Mountain and Mount Talbert are zoned as open space.

Residents voted to incorporate on August 25, 1965, by 111 to 66, when about 300 people lived here. The city has grown fast since then.

Population was 1,519 in 1990, 4,519 in 2000, 13,903 in 2010 and 23,733 in 2020, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 28,916.

Much of the housing dates from that growth run. In the 2020 census, 78.5 percent of occupied housing was owner-occupied and 44.2 percent of households had children under 18. A lot of houses built during that run are reaching the age when roofs, water heaters and exterior paint come due, so a buyer's inspection may flag them.

After voters dissolved the City of Damascus in May 2016, more than 1,000 acres, mostly in the western part of the old city, were voluntarily annexed into Happy Valley. Whether a parcel sits inside city limits or still in the county changes the yearly tax bill, and buyers ask about it early.

The city's own rate is $0.67 per $1,000 of assessed value. The city's estimates of what annexation adds are below.

Where the parcel sits nowAdded tax if annexed, per $1,000 of assessed value
Urban unincorporated Clackamas CountyAbout $1.34
Former Damascus areaAbout $2.04

The city adds that annexing owners get around-the-clock police coverage, four code enforcement officers and city public works services, and there is no annexation fee. The Clackamas County Assessment and Taxation office can confirm exact numbers for your parcel.

Pleasant Valley and North Carver is a planning area of about 2,700 acres east and south of the existing neighborhoods, set aside for future homes and jobs. The plan covers roads, parks, schools, sewer and water together. Clackamas County Water Environment Services handles sewer planning, and Sunrise Water Authority handles water.

New subdivisions here will compete with resale homes elsewhere in town for the same buyers, so look at what is under construction near you. The city has also run the Happy Valley Library since July 2015, and an expansion of more than 10,000 square feet broke ground in 2023. Mention amenities like that when you describe the neighborhood.

Commercial and mixed-use buildings follow an architectural style the city calls Happy Valley Style, a modern Cascadia look drawing on craftsman, prairie and rustic designs. The city adopted a comprehensive plan before the Metro urban growth boundary was drawn in 1978, and a single zoning map ties land use to that plan.

  • Developers often must build or upgrade water and sewer lines, roads, trails and parks at their own cost.
  • Scouters Mountain and Mount Talbert Nature Parks stay protected as open space.
  • Master-planned neighborhoods include Taralon, Jackson Hills and The Reserve.

If your house is in a master-planned community, ask your title company early about homeowners association dues and transfer fees, since those vary by community.

The area gets about 48 inches of rain a year, which is high for the Portland region. Roofs, gutters and drainage deserve a look before any buyer inspection, and hillside lots can need retaining or drainage work after a wet year. Document anything you have already repaired, since an inspector will notice both the fix and the problem. Keep receipts together so you can answer questions without hunting for paperwork.

Sunnyside Road is the main commercial street, and the Highway 212 corridor just east of town is one of the state's busiest east-west freight routes. Clackamas County, ODOT, Metro and the city have a Sunrise Corridor plan covering safer streets, walking and biking links, green space and river access east of the city.

Most of the city is in the North Clackamas School District, which runs two high schools, two middle schools and eight elementary schools here. Parts of the planning area fall in Centennial and Gresham-Barlow. Check the district for your exact address.

Clackamas County property tax is paid in three parts, due November 15, February 15 and May 15. When a due date lands on a weekend, the next business day applies. In 2025 the first date shifted to November 17 for that reason.

Paying in full by the first date earns a 3 percent discount, and two-thirds earns 2 percent. Value appeals go to the Property Value Appeals Board, and the deadline falls each year on December 31. The county posts its yearly notice on the Assessment and Taxation pages, and your closing agent will split the current year between you and the buyer.

An Oregon seller delivers a written property disclosure to a buyer who makes a written offer, and the buyer then has a limited window to revoke. The form covers what you know about the house, so list past leaks, repairs and permits.

At closing, the title company pays off your mortgage and any unpaid tax, divides the current year's tax, and records the deed with Clackamas County. Ask for estimated numbers in writing before you sign.

If the house is in a master-planned community, ask the title officer to request any association resale paperwork right away, because it can take a few days to arrive. If the parcel recently moved into the city, bring any annexation paperwork you received so the tax rate is clear to everyone involved.

sections.h2: What Happy Valley sellers tend to run into
sections.html:
• Annexation questions: buyers want to know which tax rate applies.
  • Newer construction nearby: fresh builds set the standard buyers expect.
  • Slopes and rain: hillside lots can need drainage or retaining work after a wet year.
  • Community rules: master-planned neighborhoods can carry association dues and resale paperwork.

sections.h2: Selling for cash in Happy Valley
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval and lets you choose a closing date that fits a move or an estate timeline. Ask for the terms in writing, compare them to the cost of prep and listing, and decide from there.

We buy houses in Happy Valley as they are, so you can skip painting, staging and showings. Request an offer online or by phone when you are ready.

faqs.q: What county is Happy Valley, Oregon in?
faqs.a: Happy Valley is in Clackamas County, about 13 miles southeast of downtown Portland. Property tax bills and recording go through Clackamas County.

faqs.q: When did Happy Valley become a city?
faqs.a: Residents voted to incorporate on August 25, 1965, by 111 to 66. About 300 people lived in the community at the time.

faqs.q: How many people live in Happy Valley?
faqs.a: The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 28,916 residents. The 2020 census counted 23,733 and the 2010 census 13,903.

faqs.q: Does annexation raise property taxes in Happy Valley?
faqs.a: Yes. The city estimates about $1.34 more per $1,000 of assessed value for urban unincorporated Clackamas County and about $2.04 more for the former Damascus area, with the city's own rate at $0.67 per $1,000. Confirm exact numbers with Clackamas County.

faqs.q: When are Clackamas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15, with the next business day counting if a date falls on a weekend. A full payment by the first date earns a 3 percent discount.
